content:
The Rhodes Scholarship is the oldest and best-known international graduate award in the world: full funding for a degree at the University of Oxford, a global community of roughly a hundred new scholars each year, and a selection process that rewards leadership as much as academics. For the 2027 class, applications run through the Rhodes House online portal, with constituency deadlines typically falling between June and October 2026 depending on your region.

What the scholarship covers

  • All university and college fees for one, occasionally two, Oxford master's degrees or the DPhil (doctorate)
  • A generous annual living stipend — in the region of £19,000+ per year, set each cycle by Rhodes House (confirm the current figure on the official page)
  • Two economy flights: to Oxford at the start and home at the end
  • Arrival allowance and settling-in support in Oxford
  • Access to the Rhodes community, leadership programmes, and alumni networks (scholars routinely describe these as the real prize)

Who is eligible

RequirementDetail
AgeTypically 19–27 on 1 October of entry year (a few constituencies allow older candidates — check yours)
DegreeA bachelor's degree (or completing one) by October 2027, strong academic record
Citizenship/residencyApply through your constituency (Pakistan, India, East Africa, Southern Africa, US, Canada, Australia, Syria-Jordan-Lebanon-Palestine, and more)
EnglishOxford's English-language requirements apply; waivers exist for English-taught degrees
LeadershipDemonstrated commitment to making a difference — the heart of the selection criteria

The five selection criteria

  1. Academic excellence — strong enough to win an Oxford place in your subject.
  2. Energy to use your talents fully — sport, music, debate, entrepreneurship: depth beats breadth.
  3. Truth, courage, devotion to duty — integrity and moral force.
  4. Moral force of character and instinct to lead — evidence you have taken responsibility for others.
  5. Fellowship — will you contribute to and draw from the scholar community?

Selection committees read for evidence: a paragraph describing an initiative you led beats a page of adjectives. Structure your personal statement around two or three concrete stories — see our personal statement guide for structure, then push it further than a degree application.

Timeline for the 2027 class

StageTypical window
Applications openAround June 2026 (varies by constituency)
Constituency deadlinesJuly – October 2026 (many fall late September / early October)
Shortlisting & socialsOctober – November 2026
Final interviewsNovember – December 2026 (most constituencies)
Offers and Oxford course applicationsDecember 2026 onward
Arrival in OxfordOctober 2027

Deadlines differ by constituency by weeks, and a few (like the newly opened global constituencies) run later — the official page lists every deadline. Treat the table as the pattern, not the rule.

[[chart:rhodes-timeline]]

How to build a competitive application

  • Start 4–6 months early: reference letters (5–8 for Rhodes) take months to organize — use our request templates early.
  • Choose the Oxford course deliberately: one-year master's vs DPhil changes the interview conversation — see our UK applications guide.
  • Prepare for the interview like a job assessment: expect questions on your statement, current affairs in your region, and what you would do with the fellowship — our interview guide covers the mechanics.
  • Rejected once? Reapply. Rhodes explicitly welcomes reapplicants; a stronger, more specific application the second time routinely wins.

Questions applicants often ask

Can Pakistanis apply? Yes — Pakistan has its own constituency with dedicated scholarships; the same applies to India, Bangladesh (through the SAARC arrangements where listed), East Africa and more. Check the official constituency list.

Is there an age limit? The standard window is 19–27, but some constituencies extend it — read your constituency's page carefully.

DPhil or master's? Both are fundable; most scholars start with a one- or two-year master's and some continue to the DPhil with extended funding.

What happens after selection

  1. Offer and constituency confirmation (Nov–Dec 2026): you accept through the portal.
  2. Oxford course application: apply to your chosen Oxford programme by the January 2027 deadlines (Rhodes scholars apply with the university's standard graduate deadlines — Rhodes House guides you through this).
  3. Visa and funding paperwork: spring 2027; the Rhodes office initiates CAS/visa documentation.
  4. Arrival: early October 2027, with the international scholars' orientation before term.

Statements that win: three patterns

  • The trajectory pattern: one thread (e.g. education access in your region) from age 16 to now — each step a bigger version of the last, Oxford as the bridge to what's next.
  • The pivot pattern: a technical degree, a formative exposure to the problem you now want to solve, and a precise reason why Oxford's specific people/centres finish the arc.
  • The builder pattern: things you started and ran (organizations, campaigns, platforms) with numbers attached. Rhodes loves founders — as long as the grades back it up.

Whatever the pattern, name two or three Oxford-specific resources (a centre, a professor's work, a college's community) and be equally specific about returning value to your home region. For the mechanics of the writing itself, our personal statement examples and academic gap guide cover structure and tricky histories.

Competition in numbers

Roughly a hundred scholarships are awarded each year across more than twenty constituencies, from over ten thousand applications worldwide. Per-constituency odds vary enormously: the largest constituencies (US, India, Southern Africa) field hundreds of applicants per seat, while smaller ones can be single-digit competitions. Your only lever is fit and specificity — apply where you genuinely belong.
